chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Baraqi, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid al-Attar, from Abu Sa'id al-Makari, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man killed a lion in the Haram (sanctuary). He (AS) said: Upon him is a sheep that he must slaughter. The ruling is that we hold him liable because he killed it, even if he did not intend it, for if the matter is thus, the expiation becomes obligatory upon him.
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for accidentally killing a lion in the Haram?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Isfabar, Imam al-Sadiq (as) clarifies that the expiation (kaffarah) for killing a lion in the Haram is a sheep, establishing that the liability applies even if the act was unintentional (ghayr mu'tamid). This ruling highlights the specific sanctity of the Haram's wildlife and the principle that accidental killing within the sacred precincts still incurs a religious penalty, distinct from general accidental death rulings.
